$comment: sandbox-breach control plane. Two projects, one per A/B leg, so the same unmodified
OpenClaw/Claude-Code-in-OpenShell-sandbox agent and the same memory-recall exploit route to
two different backends purely by which roundhouse turn key it is handed -- nothing in the
agent, the skill, or the exploit payload changes between legs. 'sandbox-breach-local' allows
Neither project uses '*' on purpose: this demo's point is to show the SAME exploit succeeding
identically regardless of which model authored the poisoned tool-call arguments, so each leg's
policy should refuse to silently fall over to the other backend.
The turn key's SECRET is never in this file -- only sha256(secret). Run mint_keys.py to fill in
the key_sha256 fields; it writes the plain secrets to keys.local.json (gitignored).
credentials.providers.nvidia-inference-api.env_var names the variable the server reads at
startup (INFERENCE_API_KEY) -- it must be exported or the server refuses to load, even for the
local-only project, because the catalog's one frontier entry still needs a provider cross-check
to pass (see openjev-demo's control-plane.json $comment for the same reasoning).
